title: Hogmanay in Edinburgh 2026: dates, tickets and what to book
author: Brogan
cover_image_alt: Edinburgh's Old Town rooftops, church spires and the castle on its rock under a cloudy sky
intro: Edinburgh's Hogmanay 2026 runs from 29 December to 1 January, with a torchlight procession, a warm-up gig, the Street Party and fireworks from the castle at midnight. Here's what's on each day, what needs a ticket, and how to plan a three or four-night trip.
seo_title: Hogmanay in Edinburgh 2026: dates, tickets and tips
seo_description: 29 Dec to 1 Jan: torchlight procession, The Fratellis on the 30th, Underworld and the Street Party on the 31st, Loony Dook on New Year's Day. What to book.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Dates:** 29 Dec 2026 to 1 Jan 2027
- **Big night:** Thursday 31 December
- **Street Party:** about £39, age 12+
- **Gardens headliner:** Underworld
- **How long:** 3 or 4 nights

Hogmanay is the Scottish name for New Year's Eve, and Edinburgh throws the best-known party of all. The main events are ticketed and some sell out, so book tickets before you book a hotel, and book the hotel early.

sections.heading: What's on, day by day
sections.text:
| Date | Event | Ticket? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tue 29 Dec | Torchlight Procession | To carry a torch |
| Wed 30 Dec | Night Afore Party with The Fratellis | Yes, from about £42 |
| Thu 31 Dec | Street Party on Princes Street | Yes, about £39 |
| Thu 31 Dec | Hogmanay in the Gardens with Underworld | Yes, from about £79 |
| Fri 1 Jan | Loony Dook at South Queensferry | Free to watch |

These were the published plans when we checked in October 2026. Times and line-ups can change, so check the official Edinburgh's Hogmanay website before you travel, and buy tickets only from the sellers it lists.

sections.heading: 29 December: the Torchlight Procession
sections.text:
The festival opens with thousands of people carrying flaming torches through the Old Town after dark, with pipe bands, drummers and, in many years, Up Helly Aa Vikings from Shetland. It's one of the most striking things you can see in Scotland in winter.

You need a wristband to carry a torch, but watching from the pavement is free. Find a spot along the route early, as the pavements fill up fast.

Tip: arrive on the 29th if you can. The procession is the most atmospheric part of the festival, and it's a much calmer evening than the 31st.

sections.heading: 30 December: the Night Afore Party
sections.text:
The night before Hogmanay is a big outdoor gig in West Princes Street Gardens, below the castle. For 2026 the headliners are **The Fratellis**, the Glasgow band behind "Chelsea Dagger", marking 20 years since their first album. Doors are in the early evening, so you can still go for dinner afterwards.

It's a good choice if you want live music without the crowds and the late finish of the 31st.

sections.heading: 31 December: the Street Party and the fireworks
sections.text:
On Hogmanay itself, the centre of the city becomes one huge ticketed party. You have two main choices:

- **The Street Party:** Princes Street is closed to traffic and filled with stages, DJs and food stalls, with the castle lit up above. It's the classic choice, with tens of thousands of people.
- **Hogmanay in the Gardens:** a concert in West Princes Street Gardens, right under the castle. For 2026 the headliners are **Underworld**, who'll play a live soundtrack to the midnight fireworks, including "Born Slippy" from Trainspotting.

At midnight the fireworks are fired from Edinburgh Castle, and then everyone links arms for "Auld Lang Syne", the Robert Burns song now sung around the world.

Both events are for **ages 12 and over**, so they don't suit younger children. If you're travelling with little ones, see the free options below.

Watch out: Hogmanay is outdoors in a Scottish winter. In 2024, the Street Party, the concert and the fireworks were all cancelled on the day because of high winds. Check the refund terms when you buy, and keep an eye on the forecast.
sections.image_alt: The unfinished stone columns of the National Monument on Calton Hill in snow, with low winter sun behind
sections.image_caption: Calton Hill, a short walk from Princes Street, is one of the best viewpoints in the city.

sections.heading: 1 January: the Loony Dook and First Footin'
sections.text:
On New Year's Day, hundreds of people in fancy dress parade through South Queensferry and run into the freezing Firth of Forth, right under the Forth Bridge. This is the Loony Dook, and it's free to watch. South Queensferry is about 30 minutes from the city centre by bus or train to Dalmeny. Check the organiser's times for 2027 before you go.

Back in the city, the festival usually ends with a day of free or cheap music in small venues around the Old Town, called First Footin'. It's named after the old tradition of being the first person through a friend's door after midnight, carrying a gift such as shortbread, whisky or a lump of coal for luck.

sections.heading: Hogmanay without a ticket
sections.text:
You don't need a ticket to enjoy Hogmanay in Edinburgh. The fireworks from the castle can be seen from all over the city, and the rest of the festival week is full of free things to do.

- **Watch the procession** on 29 December from the pavement.
- **See the fireworks from a hill** outside the ticketed area. Calton Hill, Blackford Hill and Inverleith Park are popular, but check whether any are closed or ticketed this year.
- **Go to a ceilidh**, a Scottish folk dance where a caller teaches every step. Many pubs and halls hold them over New Year.
- **Walk up Arthur's Seat** on New Year's Day for a clear head and a view over the city and the sea.

Local knowledge: don't climb Arthur's Seat in the dark to watch the fireworks. The paths are steep, unlit and often icy, and people are hurt on it every winter.

sections.heading: Hogmanay outside Edinburgh
sections.text:
Edinburgh is the biggest party, but Scotland has older and stranger traditions too.

- **Stonehaven Fireballs:** in this harbour town south of Aberdeen, about 40 people swing balls of fire around their heads down the High Street just before midnight, then throw them into the sea.
- **Biggar Bonfire:** a huge bonfire is lit in the middle of this small town in South Lanarkshire on New Year's Eve.
- **A Highland lodge or cottage:** many people see in the year quietly with a log fire, a ceilidh in the village hall and a long walk on New Year's Day.

These are small community events rather than visitor festivals, so check this year's plans locally before you plan a trip around them.

sections.heading: Getting there and where to stay
sections.text:
Edinburgh is easy to reach from most of the UK.

- **By train:** from London King's Cross, direct trains take about four and a half hours. Book early, as trains on the 29th and 30th fill up, and check for engineering works over the holidays.
- **By plane:** flights from London take about an hour and a quarter, and the tram from [Edinburgh Airport](/blog/how-early-should-you-arrive-at-edinburgh-airport) runs into the centre in about 35 minutes.
- **Where to stay:** the Old Town and New Town put you within walking distance of everything. Leith, by the water, is a little cheaper and a short tram ride away.

Hotel prices for the 30th and 31st are some of the highest of the year, and many places have a three-night minimum. Book as soon as you've chosen your tickets.

It's cold and dark. In late December the sun sets at about 3.40pm, and daytime highs are usually around 5 to 7°C, with wind and rain more likely than snow. Bring a warm, waterproof coat and comfortable shoes for standing outside for hours.

sections.heading: Is Hogmanay in Edinburgh right for you?
sections.text:
Choose Edinburgh if you want a **big, famous New Year's Eve** with real traditions, a stunning setting, and no flight needed for most of the UK. Choose somewhere else if you want guaranteed good weather, if you're bringing children under 12 to the main events, or if crowds aren't your thing.

For fireworks in the warm, [Madeira](/destinations/madeira) is hard to beat, and [Reykjavik](/destinations/reykjavik) has bonfires and fireworks set off all over the city. Our [New Year holidays](/destinations/new-year-holidays) page has more ideas, near and far. If everyone wants something different, put a few options in a draw on [somewhere.party](/) and let it decide.

faqs.question: When is Hogmanay in Edinburgh in 2026?
faqs.answer: Edinburgh's Hogmanay runs from 29 December 2026 to 1 January 2027. The Street Party and the midnight fireworks are on Thursday 31 December.

faqs.question: How much are Edinburgh Hogmanay Street Party tickets?
faqs.answer: About £39 for a standard ticket in 2026, with a cheaper price for Edinburgh residents. Hogmanay in the Gardens with Underworld starts at about £79.

faqs.question: Can children go to the Edinburgh Hogmanay Street Party?
faqs.answer: No, not young children. The Street Party and Hogmanay in the Gardens are for ages 12 and over. The torchlight procession and the fireworks from outside the ticketed area are open to everyone.

faqs.question: Can you see the Edinburgh Hogmanay fireworks for free?
faqs.answer: Yes. The fireworks are fired from Edinburgh Castle and can be seen from hills and parks around the city, such as Calton Hill, Blackford Hill and Inverleith Park, as long as they aren't closed that year.

faqs.question: What is the Loony Dook?
faqs.answer: A New Year's Day tradition where people in fancy dress run into the freezing Firth of Forth at South Queensferry, under the Forth Bridge. It's free to watch.
